flags.text: The bar's colour stops and labels do not line up with the bands the badge uses. Four equal gradient stops over 0–1.5 put the 'Threshold' colour at α1 0.5 and 'Aerobic' at 1.0, not at the 0.5/0.75/1.0 boundaries the doc comment lists. The centred 'Threshold' label sits at α1 0.75, which is exactly where the badge switches to 'Easy' (LiveDFAAnalyzer.Band.display). So α1 ≈ 0.8 shows an 'Easy' badge with the dot next to 'Threshold'.

Attaches a zero-distance DragGesture: on change it calls startHolding unless finalizing, and on end it calls cancelHolding. Also sets VoiceOver label/hint by finalizing state and an 'End workout now' accessibility action that calls onStop directly unless finalizing.
units.entry: DragGesture onChanged/onEnded and VoiceOver custom action
calls: closure:onStop — set by FitnessTabView.stateBody to FitnessTabView.stopAction(for:) → Task{ await recorder.stop() }

branches.effect: true: return (no hold started; note startHolding's own warning-haptic path is therefore unreachable from here); false: startHolding()
hint 'Saving in progress' vs 'Press and hold for 1.2 s…'

flags.text: The gesture returns early while finalizing (line 484), so startHolding's isFinalizing branch (warning haptic, lines 587-591) never runs. A second hold while saving gets no feedback, although the comment at 582-584 promises a warning haptic.

cancelHolding runs only from the DragGesture's .onEnded. Nothing resets the hold on gesture cancellation: there is no @GestureState, no .onDisappear and no timer invalidation outside cancelHolding/advanceHold in either file. SwiftUI does not call onEnded for a cancelled gesture (for example a system interruption mid-press, or the view leaving the hierarchy). The repeating 50 ms timer on RunLoop.main then keeps filling holdProgress and calls completeHold → onStop() → recorder.stop(), ending the workout without a completed hold.

180 pt map card: a constant backdrop, then the waiting placeholder when there are no coordinates or the live map otherwise. Overlays the GPS accuracy badge and reframes the camera when the coordinate count changes.

flags.text: Map framing only runs from .onChange(of: coordinates.count), which does not fire for the initial value. When the card mounts with points already present (it mounts ~50 ms after start, and again after navigating away and back), the camera stays .automatic until the count changes.

units.does: Shows a 'GPS ±Nm' capsule when horizontal accuracy is worse than 20 m.
Recentres the camera on the first fix (200 m region), then on the whole-track bounding region whenever the track has grown by ≥10 points since the last framing.

branches.effect: false: return; true: record count and frame

flags.text: If the coordinate count ever drops below lastFramedCount (e.g. the track array is replaced), newCount − lastFramedCount is negative. Reframing then stops until the track grows 10 past the old high-water mark.

WorkoutLocationManager seeds the track with a rejected (inaccurate) fix and later replaces it with track = [location], so the count stays 1. onChange(of: coordinates.count) does not fire and the camera stays on the 200 m region around the seed, which the code says 'may sit hundreds of metres off'. The +10 rule then keeps it there until the track reaches 11 points (lastFramedCount = 1).

units.does: Bounding region for the track via MapBoundsHelper.region(for:).
